subject: Clarify SKU passback, reseller fee, and SKU harmonization for GCP private offer
messages:
From: Julia Kim <julia.kim@acme.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on GCP private offer — SKU mapping & passback

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has started drafting the private offer and a few items popped up that we need clarified before we proceed:

- The pricing spreadsheet lists two GCP SKUs (redwood-g-stand-1 and redwood-g-stand-2). We're unclear which SKU maps to your standard and premium usage buckets for committed spend.
- For channel passback: our reseller requires a clear line item showing the 10% reseller fee as a passthrough. The private offer template from Marketplace doesn't have a dedicated passback line — will Redwood accept a 10% reseller passback off list price?
- There is also a request from our finance team about how overage credits would flow if we exceed committed units in Q1. They asked for an example proforma.

Can you please confirm SKU mapping, whether the 10% passback is acceptable, and attach a sample proforma? If you prefer a quick call, Julia and I are available Wednesday morning.

Best,
Julia
Julia Kim
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Enterprise
procurement@acme.com

Attachments: none
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Julia Kim <julia.kim@acme.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on GCP private offer — SKU mapping & passback

Julia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, details below and a proforma attached.

- SKU mapping: redwood-g-stand-1 -> standard inference (4 vCPU equiv, single-GPU); redwood-g-stand-2 -> premium inference (larger memory, multi-GPU routing for long-context). I'll attach a short SKU matrix that maps expected latency and token throughput so you can tie it to your consumption forecast.
- Reseller passback: we can support an explicit 10% pass-through line in the private offer, but we need to reflect that in the net revenue waterfall for both Redwood and the GCP billing entry. Operationally we'll set the Marketplace listing list-price to include the passback and stamp a separate invoice line for the reseller.
- Overage credits: we can include a quarterly smoothing credit: if Q1 overage exceeds 5% of committed units, we will apply an overage credit equal to the per-token list rate multiplied by the excess usage, capped at 2% of the quarterly commit. Example is in the proforma.

Action plan:
1) I attached the proforma (Redwood_PO_proforma_v3.pdf) and the SKU mapping (SKU_bucket_matrix.xlsx).
2) Ben — can you confirm the channel margin Math below and whether we can accept the 10% passback without impacting the committed price?
3) Laura — I'll put together the Marketplace private-offer draft (with an explicit passback line) and share for signature.

If that works, we can run a short call Wed 10am PT to finalize.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_PO_proforma_v3.pdf (proforma, 3 pages); SKU_bucket_matrix.xlsx (SKU mapping, 1 sheet)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on GCP private offer — SKU mapping & passback

Neha / team — ran the numbers against the proposed 10% reseller passback. Summary below.

Quick summary:
- Baseline list price (per proforma): $0.12 per 1k tokens (standard SKU) / $0.30 per 1k tokens (premium SKU).
- Proposed 10% passback lowers net realized revenue by ~9.1% after Marketplace fees (we absorb a small portion of Marketplace transaction cost).
- With the current committed unit pricing, we have ~12% gross margin headroom before hitting the minimum acceptable net revenue floor. That means a 10% passback is acceptable for Year 1 if: (a) the commit is at or above the forecasted volume in the proforma, and (b) we preserve rollover protections for unused credits for up to one quarter.

Risks / notes:
- If Acme wants to request the passback be applied to overage units rather than list — that reduces our ability to honor the committed per-unit price. Avoid applying passback to both committed and overage; we should accept passback on committed units only.
- Tax handling: passback as a separate invoice line reduces ambiguity for Acme but increases bookkeeping effort. Finance is okay with that for enterprise customers.

Recommendation: Accept the 10% reseller passback on committed units, include a quarterly rollover for unused commit (1 quarter), and cap overage credit exposure as Neha suggested. I'll feed this to legal to ensure the invoicing language is clean.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: internal calculation sheet referenced (not attached in thread)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on GCP private offer — SKU mapping & passback

FYI — drafting the private offer now. A couple of drafting points:

- I'll add a passback line item called "Reseller Pass-Through (10%)" and reference the reseller contact so accounting can route correctly.
- For the SKU rows, I'll map redwood-g-stand-1 to "Standard Inference (S)" and redwood-g-stand-2 to "Premium Inference (P)" and add clarifying notes in the attachment.
- We should avoid ambiguous language around "overage credits" — I'll use the phrasing: "Quarterly overage credit applied when usage > 105% of committed units, capped at 2% of quarterly commitment".

Neha — once I send the draft I'll include the DocuSign link for the PO.

--
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: none
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Julia Kim <julia.kim@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final private-offer framing and next steps (DocuSign link)

Julia / Acme procurement — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we've agreed to the following and attached a redlined proforma for your review:

1) SKU mapping: redwood-g-stand-1 = Standard Inference; redwood-g-stand-2 = Premium Inference (see SKU_bucket_matrix.xlsx).
2) Reseller passback: Redwood will accept a 10% reseller pass-through applied to committed units only. The private offer will show a separate invoice line labeled "Reseller Pass-Through (10%)".
3) Overage handling: Quarterly smoothing credit applies when usage > 105% of committed units; credit capped at 2% of quarterly commitment.
4) Rollover: Unused committed units may roll forward for one calendar quarter.

Next steps:
- I've shared the DocuSign envelope for the private offer here: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-PO-778
- Please countersign; procurement should expect an itemized invoice showing the passback line within 5 business days after activation.

If you'd like a 20-minute call to walk the proforma, Ben and I can join tomorrow morning.

Best,
Neha
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_PO_proforma_v3.pdf (redlined), SKU_bucket_matrix.xlsx
